record.original_question: Is the Behrend function equal to (-1)^d at every point of Hilb_d(A^3)?

evidence.quote: Problem XXVI. Is the Behrend function equal to (−1)^d for every point of Hilbd(A^3)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^3)$ denote the Hilbert scheme parametrizing zero-dimensional subschemes of length $d$ in affine 3-space $\mathbb{A}^3$ over $\mathbb{C}$. This scheme carries a symmetric obstruction theory, and hence Behrend's canonical $\mathbb{Z}$-valued constructible function $
u_X : X 	o \mathbb{Z}$ (defined for any finite-type $\mathbb{C}$-scheme $X$) takes a definite value at each closed point of $X = \mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^3)$. Recall that $
u_X(p)$ depends only on the formal neighborhood of $p$ in $X$ and that for a smooth point of an $n$-dimensional scheme $
u_X(p) = (-1)^n$.

Question: Is it true that for every integer $d \geq 1$ and every closed point $p \in \mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^3)$ one has
$$ 
u_{\mathrm{Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^3)}(p) = (-1)^d \,? $$
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative. Recent work (published in Geometry & Topology, 2025; arXiv:2311.05408) shows that Behrend's function on $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{A}^3)$ is not constant: for $n \geq 24$ there exist points where the value is $-(-1)^n$ rather than $(-1)^n$.

status_evidence.title: Behrend's function is not constant on Hilb^n(A^3)
status_evidence.snippet: For n ≥ 24 there exist points of Hilb^n(A^3) on which the Behrend function equals -(-1)^n; in particular the Behrend function is not constant.
status_evidence.claim: Disproves that the Behrend function equals (-1)^d at every point of Hilb^d(A^3).

status_evidence.title: Behrend's function is not constant on Hilb^n(A^3) — Geometry & Topology
status_evidence.snippet: Published version establishing non-constancy of the Behrend function on the Hilbert scheme of points on A^3.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms negative answer to the question in a refereed journal.
